name: contact-form-routed
title: Routed contact form
description: One form, the right team: the topic you pick changes the questions (order number for support, company size for sales) and who answers.
docs: Pass routes (an id, a label, a line on what the topic is for, its own questions as fields, and a promise of who answers and how fast), onSubmit and a title. Topic cards sit at the top as a real radio group, two across on a wide form (an odd last card takes the whole row) and one under the other on a narrow one; the questions of the chosen topic appear between email and message, in a tinted group named after the topic, and the promise under the button changes with it. A field is text, email, tel, url, date, select (options) or textarea, and may be required, carry a placeholder and a hint. Name, email and message are shared by every topic, so nothing typed in them is lost when the topic changes, and the answers to a topic's own questions are kept per topic. Focus stays on the card the reader used, and the promise is said politely to a screen reader as it changes. onSubmit receives the topic id and every answer, trimmed, keyed by field name (name, email and message are reserved). Mistakes are said in words only once a field has been visited or a send was tried, the first one takes focus, a failed send keeps everything typed, and success replaces the form with a status message that names the topic. Use route and onRouteChange to control the topic, defaultValues to prefill, defaultStatus to start in a state, privacyHref for the link under the button, and labels to translate every fixed word and error.
